title: Bound on a matching Fourier factor
statement: Let $q,k,n$ be natural numbers with $n>0$. Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose nonzero Fourier coefficients are supported only on subsets of size $k$. Given a perfect matching of the complete $q$-partite graph with $k$ vertices in each part and a specified part, assign each matching edge independently and uniformly a label from $\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. The expected square of the absolute Fourier coefficient indexed by the set of labels on the matching edges incident with that part is at most $\\frac{k!}{n^k}\\sum_{|S|=k}\\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\\widehat f(S)$ denotes the Fourier coefficient of $f$ indexed by $S$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is indexed by a set of size $k$
A perfect matching in the stated complete multipartite graph is given
A part of the graph is specified
